At 20% progress, prioritize the interpretable sampling experiment; retain temporal modeling and temperature adjustment as later alternatives.

**Insights from the supplied evidence.** (1) Users reject broad associations that miss current purpose; recent-prefix supervision could improve specificity but cannot establish compatibility. (2) Historical purchases produce redundant recommendations; subsequent-choice supervision may help, although recency can reinforce completed needs. (3) Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics have negative tenth-percentile training margins (−0.1487/−0.2356), motivating discrimination experiments. Missing training counters prevent attributing these failures to branch allocation; concentrated user spectra do not establish collapse.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690v2) uses reconstruction and additional last-item masking; exhaustive prefix enumeration is an alternative it discusses, not its prescribed procedure. (2) [RSS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) establishes recency-biased supervision, but deletes multiple sampled positions and can retain later events. Its per-draw probabilities differ from inclusion probabilities. (3) [Replicability](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07483) and [loss-comparison](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.07602) studies identify consequential convergence and objective choices; neither isolates this sampler’s effect.

The framework separates **exposure** (cutoff sampling), **temporal representation** (time-gap attention), and **discrimination** (softmax temperature). Hold optimization and evaluation fixed across each comparison.

Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder. Each assessment states a benefit and limitation.

| Atomic idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Endpoint-preserving recent-cutoff sampling | 2/6/6/6/4 | Precise, feasible exposure test targeting specificity, redundancy and weak margins | Limited novelty; recency also changes context length and target frequency |
| Learned time-gap attention bias | 4/7/6/5/6 | Encodes irregular elapsed time within BERT4Rec | Requires timestamp plumbing; elapsed time cannot identify unresolved demand |
| Moderate sampled-softmax temperature adjustment | 2/6/4/8/4 | Directly changes gradient emphasis on confusing candidates | Applicable only with an established sampled-loss control; uncertain negatives can dominate |

**Selected experiment:** endpoint-preserving recent-cutoff sampling. Establish a uniform-cutoff control with equally weighted, separately target-normalized reconstruction and strict-prefix terminal losses. Treatment changes only nonterminal cutoff probabilities. With N eligible nonterminal positions and m=min(10,N), q(endpoint)=0.1 and q(k)=0.45/N+0.45·1[k recent]/m. Length-two histories necessarily select their endpoint; when N≤10, treatment equals control.

This explicitly targets broad associations displacing current preferences, historical purchases interpreted as continuing demand, and weak lower-tail discrimination. These remain hypotheses. Historical scores 0.5850 and 0.5825 lack a verified matched comparison and cannot identify a sampling effect.

Keep baseline architecture, objective denominator, corruption, inference, seeds, splits, four routes and checkpoint selection fixed. Persist branch counts, target frequencies, context distributions and timing. Specify all resolved settings before execution; the supplied integration code cannot replace unavailable baseline source. Follow up using the same twenty users’ full-catalog recommendations for specificity and redundancy. Select only through pinned macro validation HR@10, record every evaluated configuration, and treat small adaptive wins as provisional. Sampling shortcuts and fixed-budget convergence differences require measured investigation; neither training probes nor sampled validation establish full-catalog suitability.

idea.description: Run a controlled endpoint-preserving recent-cutoff sampling experiment within the supplied corrected BERT4Rec. Establish the uniform-cutoff control first; then train a separate treatment changing only conditional nonterminal cutoff probabilities. Each trial trains one jointly optimized model per category, and deployment uses exactly one selected checkpoint per category. Retain temporal attention and temperature adjustment as subsequent, separately budgeted alternatives rather than simultaneous additions.
idea.motivation: The experiment addresses two observed user failures: broad associations displacing specific current preferences, and previous purchases being interpreted as continuing demand. Strict-prefix next-choice supervision learns observed subsequent choices; recent cutoff sampling increases exposure to recent contexts. Neither mechanism guarantees recognition of completed needs, compatibility, quantity suitability, or mood. Negative lower-tail sampled training margins in Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics motivate testing discrimination, but do not identify its cause. Concentrated user representation spectra are descriptive evidence, not proof of collapse or causality. At 20% research progress, this limited intervention is more interpretable than introducing temporal architecture, text encoding or hard-negative mining before establishing a matched control.
idea.implementation_notes:
Baseline integration and attribution: The supplied input contains no baseline source, so the code is an integration component rather than a replacement train.py. Integrate it into the supplied corrected baseline sampler and training loop while preserving its helpers, diagnosis adapter and embedded predictor writer. Verify the actual baseline objective and resolved configuration before execution. If the baseline does not already implement the two-branch objective, establishing that objective is a separate control-building intervention. Attribute only the subsequent matched control-versus-treatment difference to cutoff sampling. Historical reported scores 0.5850 and 0.5825 do not establish that comparison or a statistically reliable improvement.

Prior-art distinction: Original BERT4Rec specifies masked reconstruction, additional last-item-only examples and appended-MASK inference. It discusses every-prefix next-item training as an expensive alternative, not its prescribed procedure. Its official generator uses overlapping windows, random-mask copies and a last-item-only example per window. Its default selected-token replacement is MASK, despite inherited 80/10/10 comments. The paper describes item-only softmax, whereas official executable code includes special embedding rows in normalization. Preserve the corrected host baseline's actual convention rather than silently replacing it with either interpretation. RSS establishes recency-biased supervision but samples multiple positions with replacement, collapses duplicate positions into a set and deletes them while retaining other events, potentially including events after a target. RSS therefore does not implement the proposed single-cutoff strict-prefix construction or reserved endpoint probability. Its per-draw normalization is not loss normalization, and position inclusion probabilities differ from per-draw probabilities.

Eligibility and inputs: Establish both branches with the same eligible users: histories containing at least two training events. Retain the baseline user-sampling distribution conditional on that eligibility rule and count excluded users. Keep baseline reconstruction corruption and guarantee at least one valid reconstruction target per example through the same documented procedure in both arms. Terminal inputs contain only events preceding the selected target occurrence plus the reserved MASK; exclude that occurrence and all subsequent events. Earlier occurrences of its item ID remain legitimate context. Reconstruction must never expose shifted prediction labels through bidirectional input. Preserve repeated positions and their targets. Require maxlen >= 2 and retain at most maxlen-1 context events before the appended MASK.

Loss reduction: For each optimizer step use loss = 0.5 * reconstruction_sum / reconstruction_target_count + 0.5 * terminal_sum / terminal_target_count. Each sum contains valid individual target losses under the unchanged baseline CE convention. Reconstruction therefore averages over targets across the branch, not first within each sequence; sequences with more masked targets contribute more reconstruction weight. Terminal examples each contribute one target. Empty branches must raise an error. Preserve baseline class denominators, special-token handling, label mapping, embedding tying, negative sampling, collision handling and sampling correction. Ignoring padded target labels does not by itself remove PAD or MASK logits from normalization. Do not add historical-item negative exclusions or change full-softmax/sampled-loss conventions during this comparison. Uncorrected sampled candidate CE must not be called equivalent to corrected sampled softmax.

Cutoff distribution: Use zero-based event indices. For history length n > 2, eligible nonterminal target indices are 1 through n-2; let N=n-2 and m=min(10,N). The control assigns endpoint probability 0.1 and probability 0.9/N to each nonterminal cutoff. Treatment assigns endpoint probability 0.1 and unconditional nonterminal probability 0.45/N + 0.45/m for recent-window indices, or 0.45/N otherwise. The recent window excludes the endpoint. These probabilities sum to one. For n=2, the endpoint is the sole eligible target and receives probability one; count this exception. Histories shorter than two events are ineligible. Treatment and control coincide whenever N<=10, so record the fraction of eligible histories and sampled batches where the policies can differ. This is event-position recency, not elapsed-time decay. Reconstruction may additionally supervise the endpoint, so total endpoint supervision and coefficient mass are not fixed at 0.1.

Reproducibility: Preserve preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42. Both arms should use the same documented data RNG scheme: NumPy SeedSequence([42, category_id, epoch, batch_id, purpose_id]), category IDs 0 through 3 in the supplied category order, and purpose IDs 0=user selection, 1=cutoffs, 2=reconstruction corruption, 3=negative sampling. Introducing this scheme changes original baseline random draws and must be disclosed. Match user draws and cutoff uniforms across arms, transforming the same cutoff uniform through each policy's inverse CDF. Keep model initialization/dropout RNG separate from data RNG; explicitly seed worker libraries and provide a dedicated DataLoader torch.Generator if workers are used. Keep shapes and forward-call order matched where feasible. Shared uniforms do not guarantee identical realized masks or cross-platform determinism. Record library versions, hardware and determinism settings.

Resolved execution settings: Preserve maximum 200 epochs, exactly 200 batches per executed epoch, the SASREC_EPOCHS environment behavior capped at 200, single-GPU execution, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts and all four dataset routes. Specify the same batch size, maximum history length, architecture, initialization, optimizer, learning rate schedule, weight decay, reconstruction policy, negative count if applicable, validation schedule and checkpoint-selection rule in both arms before running. Reuse the supplied values; none can be inferred from absent baseline code. Save one selected checkpoint per category without averaging. Controls, treatment, diagnostics, debugging and failures share the 43,200 GPU-second search budget. Measure elapsed time and completed optimizer steps; do not claim equal wall-clock cost. Fixed-budget results may reflect convergence speed as well as eventual modeling quality, and the 200-epoch cap must remain unchanged.

Training measurements: Persist epoch and cumulative branch example counts, valid target counts, coefficient masses, target-weighted CE, endpoint selections and exceptions, excluded users, expected and realized cutoff probabilities, context-length distributions, target frequencies, policy-distinguishable history counts and timing alongside each checkpoint. Restore counters explicitly for diagnosis; a state_dict alone does not preserve runtime bookkeeping. Each nonempty branch contributes coefficient mass 0.5 per step, but this is neither its loss-value share nor its gradient share. Diagnostic-loader terminal-position coverage cannot reconstruct training branch allocation.

Diagnostic and predictor contracts: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), family-specific sample_batch and all ModelView interfaces. view.model must be the actual trained nn.Module; preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. The diagnostic loader continues yielding (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B x L; adapt probes to actual masked-target BERT4Rec inputs rather than assuming shifted causal targets. This sampler change requires no inference architecture change: preserve appended-MASK inference and maximum-nonpadding-index readout, never nonpadding_count-1. Each category loads exactly one independently trained checkpoint. Never combine experimental arms, checkpoints, independently fitted experts or separately fitted scores. Preserve the embedded predictor writer and category routing; any later architecture change must update both training and writer together.

Validation and qualitative assessment: Select with the unchanged host macro validation HR@10: 200 validation users per category, 99 unique negative candidates and evaluation seed 42. Retain fixed splits and evaluator; never inspect hidden test files or use test metrics. If aligned per-user binary hits are supplied, report paired gained/lost hits and optionally bootstrap 200 users with replacement within each category for 10,000 replicates, using the same indices for both arms and analysis seed 42. Average the four category differences equally and report the observed difference and percentile 95% interval. Otherwise omit the interval rather than reconstructing unavailable hits. One additional hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. Such intervals condition on fitted models and fixed candidates; they exclude training randomness, alternative negatives and adaptive-selection optimism. Record all evaluated configurations, checkpoint-selection rules and evaluation counts. Treat small adaptive validation wins as provisional.

Use the same twenty real training users, five per category, for separate full-catalog unseen-item qualitative recommendations. Track willingness to choose supported by a specific current purpose, and rejection reasons involving duplication, staleness, specifications, quantity, unsupported projects, mood or seasonal mismatch. Track uncertainty for unidentified items rather than inventing suitability labels. Use only histories and supplied timestamps, titles and descriptions. Unavailable ratings, review text, item categories, prices, stores and simulator traits remain unavailable despite generic metadata examples.

Shortcut learning and interpretation: Recent cutoffs can change target popularity, repeated-purchase exposure, retained context length and short-lived preferences. Inspect these distributions using training data; do not infer frequency-stratified improvements when results are unavailable. The primary comparison estimates the total sampling-policy effect and cannot isolate recency from these mediators. Do not reverse-weight treatment losses by cutoff probabilities, because that would change the intended exposure intervention. A later, separately budgeted context-matched control could hold retained context length fixed, acknowledging changed eligibility. Time-gap attention, temperature, endpoint probability, branch weights and negative mining remain separate future ablations. Temperature adjustment is appropriate only after specifying an actual sampled-loss control; time-aware attention would require a history-only timestamp reference for the appended mask and a matching predictor. Neither training margins nor sampled validation establish full-catalog suitability or resolution of current needs.
idea.pseudocode:
import os
import numpy as np
import torch

DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']
CATEGORIES = (
    'Movies_and_TV', 'Industrial_and_Scientific',
    'Electronics', 'CDs_and_Vinyl',
)
USER, CUTOFF, CORRUPTION, NEGATIVE = range(4)


def data_rng(category_id, epoch, batch_id, purpose_id):
    return np.random.default_rng(np.random.SeedSequence(
        [42, category_id, epoch, batch_id, purpose_id]))


def cutoff_probabilities(n, treatment=False):
    # Entry j corresponds to target event index j+1.
    # Only training histories enter this function.
    if n < 2:
        raise ValueError('Terminal sampling requires at least two events')
    if n == 2:
        return np.array([1.0], dtype=np.float64)
    nonterminal_count = n - 2
    probabilities = np.empty(n - 1, dtype=np.float64)
    probabilities[:-1] = 0.9 / nonterminal_count
    probabilities[-1] = 0.1
    if treatment:
        recent_count = min(10, nonterminal_count)
        probabilities[:-1] *= 0.5
        probabilities[nonterminal_count-recent_count:nonterminal_count] += (
            0.45 / recent_count)
    return probabilities


def choose_cutoff(n, u, treatment=False):
    if n < 2:
        raise ValueError('Terminal sampling requires at least two events')
    if not 0.0 <= u < 1.0:
        raise ValueError('Expected a uniform draw in [0, 1)')
    if n == 2:
        return 1, 'singleton_endpoint_exception'
    # Reserve the same endpoint region of the shared uniform in both arms.
    if u < 0.1:
        return n - 1, 'endpoint'
    nonterminal_count = n - 2
    probabilities = np.full(
        nonterminal_count, 1.0 / nonterminal_count, dtype=np.float64)
    if treatment:
        recent_count = min(10, nonterminal_count)
        probabilities *= 0.5
        probabilities[-recent_count:] += 0.5 / recent_count
    cdf = probabilities.cumsum()
    cdf[-1] = 1.0
    v = (u - 0.1) / 0.9
    j = min(int(np.searchsorted(cdf, v, side='right')),
            nonterminal_count - 1)
    return j + 1, 'nonterminal'


def terminal_batch(histories, uniforms, maxlen, mask_id, treatment=False):
    if maxlen < 2:
        raise ValueError('maxlen must retain context and MASK')
    if not histories:
        raise ValueError('A nonempty eligible batch is required')
    if len(histories) != len(uniforms):
        raise ValueError('One cutoff uniform is required per history')
    sequences = np.zeros((len(histories), maxlen), dtype=np.int64)
    targets = np.empty(len(histories), dtype=np.int64)
    records = []
    for row, (history, u) in enumerate(zip(histories, uniforms)):
        t, status = choose_cutoff(len(history), float(u), treatment)
        context = list(history[max(0, t - maxlen + 1):t])
        tokens = context + [mask_id]
        sequences[row, -len(tokens):] = tokens
        targets[row] = history[t]
        probabilities = cutoff_probabilities(len(history), treatment)
        records.append({
            'cutoff': t,
            'history_length': len(history),
            'context_length': len(context),
            'status': status,
            'target': int(history[t]),
            'expected_selected_probability': float(probabilities[t - 1]),
            'policies_can_differ': len(history) - 2 > 10,
        })
    return sequences, targets, records


def final_nonpadding_features(features, sequence):
    # Supports LEFT padding; never use nonpadding_count - 1.
    positions = torch.arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
    last = positions.unsqueeze(0).expand_as(sequence).masked_fill(
        sequence.eq(0), -1).amax(dim=1)
    if bool(last.lt(0).any()):
        raise ValueError('Cannot read out an empty sequence')
    rows = torch.arange(sequence.shape[0], device=sequence.device)
    return features[rows, last]


def balanced_loss(reconstruction_sum, reconstruction_count,
                  terminal_sum, terminal_count):
    # Sums of valid per-target losses, not means of per-sequence means.
    if reconstruction_count <= 0 or terminal_count <= 0:
        raise ValueError('Both separately normalized branches must be nonempty')
    return (0.5 * reconstruction_sum / reconstruction_count
            + 0.5 * terminal_sum / terminal_count)


def resolved_epoch_limit():
    # Preserve the host environment default and enforce its maximum.
    epochs = int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200'))
    if epochs < 1:
        raise ValueError('SASREC_EPOCHS must be positive')
    return min(epochs, 200)


# Integration specification; preserve the supplied baseline helpers.
# Preprocessing retains seed 0; initialize training with seed 42.
# Establish uniform control before a separate treatment trial.
# For each category, epoch in range(resolved_epoch_limit()), and
# batch_id in range(200):
# 1. Construct USER/CUTOFF/CORRUPTION/NEGATIVE streams with data_rng.
# 2. Sample eligible users under the shared baseline-conditional rule.
#    Record excluded users and histories where the policies can differ.
# 3. Build baseline reconstruction examples with at least one MASK target
#    per example, preserving its exact corruption and CE semantics.
# 4. Build terminal_batch with one shared cutoff uniform per sampled user.
#    Record expected distributions by history length and realized cutoffs.
# 5. Encode both branches with the SAME BERT4Rec parameters.
#    Compute reconstruction summed CE and valid target count.
#    Read terminal features at maximum nonpadding indices; compute
#    terminal summed CE and valid target count under unchanged logits.
# 6. Apply balanced_loss; zero gradients, backpropagate, update once.
# 7. Aggregate target-weighted CE, branch counts, coefficient masses,
#    cutoff/context/target-frequency counts and measured timing.
# 8. Save the checkpoint chosen by the predeclared unchanged rule,
#    resolved configuration, and epoch/cumulative counters locally.
# 9. Restore counters explicitly when loading for diagnosis.
# 10. Keep DiagnosisProbe, ModelView, family-specific sample_batch,
#     embedded predictor writer and all four routes compatible.
# Inference: append reserved MASK to retained history, left-pad, read
# its final nonpadding feature, and score candidates with that category's
# sole model. Never combine control/treatment checkpoints or scores.
# Optional paired validation analysis requires host-supplied user hits;
# bootstrap within category with identical indices across arms, seed 42,
# 10,000 replicates, and equal category averaging. Otherwise omit it.

originality.positive: The reserved endpoint probability, piecewise nonterminal distribution and strict-prefix construction define a precise operational comparison that differs from RSS's multiple-target deletion procedure.
originality.negative: Masked reconstruction, terminal masking and recency-biased supervision are established prior art. The concrete combination has limited algorithmic novelty without convincing controlled evidence.

future_potential.positive: A feasible early experiment can clarify whether exposure allocation merits later temporal representation or discrimination studies while preserving one BERT4Rec model per category.
future_potential.negative: The policy effect combines recency, context length and target exposure. It may mostly change convergence speed, and sampled validation gains may not improve current-purpose suitability or redundancy.

code_difficulty.positive: The core intervention is a small sampler change with no required architecture or inference computation change.
code_difficulty.negative: The previous score of 3 understated end-to-end work: verifying baseline loss semantics, establishing the control, matching RNG streams, persisting counters and preserving diagnostic/checkpoint contracts require careful integration. Baseline source is absent from the supplied report.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Establishes bidirectional masked-item reconstruction and additional last-item-only training examples.
Uses appended-MASK inference and its hidden state for next-item scoring.
Discusses enumerating every next-item prefix as an expensive alternative, helping distinguish the proposed sampled-prefix construction from its prescribed training procedure.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed endpoint-preserving cutoff distribution improves the pinned benchmark.
Masked prediction does not directly identify unresolved needs, compatibility or product suitability.
The paper's item-only softmax description must be distinguished from special-token normalization in executable implementations.

related_work.title: Official BERT4Rec training-data generator
contributions: Provides concrete windowing and corruption behavior: complete short histories, overlapping long-history windows, random-mask copies and an additional last-item-only example per window.
Uses a default stride of 0.1 times maximum sequence length and default selected-token mask probability 1.0.
Guarantees at least one selected target for a nonempty sequence under normal positive masking settings.
limitations: Inherited replacement comments do not necessarily describe default executable behavior.
This generator is implementation evidence, not proof of an isolated causal contribution or a mandate to replace the host sampler.

related_work.title: Official BERT4Rec output-head implementation
contributions: Shows tied embedding-based output logits normalized over all vocabulary embedding rows.
Makes explicit why ignoring padded target labels differs from removing special-token classes from the softmax denominator.
limitations: Executable normalization differs from the paper's item-only formulation.
The corrected host baseline must be checked independently; its denominator cannot be inferred from this external implementation.

related_work.title: Official BERT4Rec vocabulary implementation
contributions: Defines item and special-token vocabulary rows, yielding N+4 rows for N real items.
Together with the output-head implementation, establishes participation of special classes in executable training normalization.
limitations: Vocabulary conventions are implementation-specific and must not silently replace the supplied host token mapping.

related_work.title: Effective and Efficient Training for Sequential Recommendation using Recency Sampling
contributions: Petrov and Macdonald introduce RSS at RecSys 2022, establishing recency-biased target sampling.
Samples multiple positions with replacement using normalized recency weights, collapses duplicates into a target set and removes those positions while retaining the remaining sequence order.
Distinguishes per-draw probability from inclusion probability, which is 1-(1-p(k))^c for c draws.
Supports multiple-positive objectives and evaluates BCE and LambdaRank; connects training/inference masking mismatch to convergence.
limitations: RSS can retain interactions occurring after a target and is therefore generally different from strict-prefix terminal prediction.
The endpoint follows the same recency distribution rather than receiving reserved probability 0.1.
Sampling-probability normalization does not specify loss reduction or justify equating RSS objectives with the proposed separately normalized CE branches.

related_work.title: A Systematic Review and Replicability Study of BERT4Rec for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Petrov and Macdonald identify substantial undertraining in default BERT4Rec configurations.
Report that reproduction can require up to 30 times longer training, while their implementation reproduces three of four datasets with up to 95% less convergence time.
limitations: These findings do not establish undertraining in the supplied corrected host baseline.
They motivate reporting convergence and runtime under the fixed budget, not exceeding the required 200-epoch cap.

related_work.title: Klenitskiy and Vasilev (RecSys 2023): full-softmax and sampled-loss comparison
contributions: Demonstrates consequential accuracy and training-speed differences between full-softmax and sampled-loss choices.
Supports preserving objective semantics during a cutoff-only comparison.
limitations: Does not determine the best loss for this pinned benchmark.
Changing the loss alongside cutoff sampling would confound attribution.

related_work.title: Time Interval Aware Self-Attention for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Models pairwise time intervals alongside positional information.
Motivates a separate temporal representation experiment within the preserved BERT4Rec family.
limitations: Its architecture should not replace the required BERT4Rec backbone.
Elapsed-time modeling differs from the selected event-position sampling intervention.
Any transferred mechanism requires available timestamps and a documented history-only time reference at appended-MASK inference.

related_work.title: Wu et al. (2024): sampled-softmax analysis
contributions: Analyzes negative emphasis under sampled softmax and the role of temperature.
Motivates a later controlled discrimination experiment.
limitations: The supplied ranking analysis does not guarantee HR@10 improvements.
Changing temperature or sampling corrections would confound the selected cutoff-only comparison.
A sampled-softmax experiment requires an explicitly specified sampled-loss control and cannot be assumed to match a full-softmax baseline.
